# Distributed Scale, Observability, and Tokenomics {.unnumbered}

Part V examines agentic systems at cluster scale and operational maturity. We formalize multi-agent coordination under the Actor model, evaluate systems inside interactive reproducible software gyms (SWE-bench), instrument execution graphs with OpenTelemetry GenAI semantic conventions, and optimize fleet economics through Trajectory Goodput.

::: {#pri-vol3-stochastic-actors .callout-principle title="Distributed stochastic coordination"}

**Invariant**: Multi-agent collaboration is distributed computing over stochastic nodes subject to correlated failure; unconstrained communication incurs an $O(M^2)$ Coordination Tax.

**Implication**: Systems must use the Actor model with isolated state and hierarchical supervisor trees rather than unconstrained conversational swarms.

:::

::: {#pri-vol3-trace-reconstructibility .callout-principle title="Deterministic trace reconstructibility"}

**Invariant**: Robust production operations require capturing non-deterministic environmental interactions into immutable event streams to enable bit-exact replay and causal counterfactual diffing.

**Implication**: Runtimes must implement event-sourcing and OpenTelemetry GenAI semantic conventions across all trajectory spans.

:::

::: {#pri-vol3-trajectory-goodput .callout-principle title="Trajectory goodput and fleet economics"}

**Invariant**: The governing metric of autonomous serving is Trajectory Goodput (verified outcomes per dollar per GPU-hour), closing the data flywheel by routing verified production traces back into post-training.

**Implication**: Systems optimization follows the Improvement Ladder: exhaust runtime scaffolding and caching before distilling search into compact model weights.

:::
